subject: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@fintechco.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-20T15:10:00Z
Subject: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Hi Alex / Sara —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap of the performance discussion and proposed SLOs so we can align on next steps: 

Key targets (proposed)
- P95 latency (end-to-end, token generation): <= 200 ms
- P99 latency: <= 450 ms (for single-request, 1k token max)
- Sustained throughput: 500 requests/sec across dedicated pool
- Concurrency: support 50 concurrent long-lived streams without degradation
- Streaming: chunked streaming enabled with 50ms flush target for first tokens
- Max request size: 1,200 tokens (we recommended soft limit at 1k)

Notes / constraints we discussed:
- We suggest KV/prefix caching for repeated prefixes (chat history) to hit p95 targets at scale.
- Quantized model variant (8-bit) recommended to reduce GPU memory footprint while keeping latency SLAs — we can run a short perf sweep.

Attached: SLO_checklist.xlsx (actionable checklist), perf-results.pdf (demo perf snapshots), demo-recording.mp4

Suggested MAP (mutual action plan)
1) Redwood to run a 24h perf sweep with FinTechCo sample workload (owner: Marissa) — target: 2026-11-27
2) FinTechCo to provide representative traffic profile + sample prompt set (owner: Alex) — target: 2026-11-24
3) Redwood infra to validate streaming QoS and concurrency (owner: Aditya) — target: 2026-11-30
4) Procurement cadence & TnC review (owner: Sara) — target: 2026-12-03

Can you confirm the targets above, and that the MAP dates work for your team? Once we have the sample workload I’ll drop Aditya in to run the perf sweep and share detailed logs/metrics.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T17:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Marissa —

Thanks for the concise summary. A couple quick clarifying Qs from our infra/engineering side:

1) Streaming: when you say 50ms flush target for first tokens, is that measured from request arrival at Redwood edge to first byte delivered? We need to make sure this includes our network egress.
2) Concurrency: 50 concurrent long-lived streams — is that per-region or global? We expect our US cluster to be the primary region.
3) P99: do you have historical variance numbers for p99 when model is under burst load (e.g., 2x baseline traffic)?
4) Are there any minimum commit sizes or reserved capacity you'd recommend to guarantee the throughput target?

We’ll get you the representative traffic profile (should have it by EOD 11/24). Also looping Sara for procurement timing.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering, FinTechCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Alex — great questions, answers below and I’ve looped Aditya & Dev for technical confirmation.

1) Streaming measurement: the 50ms flush target is measured from request arrival at our edge to first byte outbound from our runtime. This does not include customer network latency — we can add a small network buffer to your SLA if you want an E2E commitment.

2) Concurrency scope: the 50 concurrent long-lived streams is per-region (US) based on the demo traffic profile you shared during the call. If you plan multi-region failover we should model peak across regions separately.

3) P99 under burst: aditya — can you confirm, but our internal perf sweeps show p99 ~ 400–550 ms during 2x baseline sustained bursts for quantized variants; p99 for FP16 tends to be lower but uses >2x memory. We’ll include the burst test in the sweep.

4) Reserved capacity: to guarantee 500 req/sec with low-latency tail guarantees we recommend a small Dedicated pool (2–3x baseline headroom) or a hybrid dedicated + burst pool. Procurement-friendly recommendation: start with 4 reserved slots in Dedicated and enable burst to shared pool for peak traffic.

Aditya / Dev — action items to confirm:
- Run 24h perf sweep using FinTechCo sample workload (include 1x and 2x sustained scenarios, streaming and non-streaming) — expected artifacts: latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), CPU/GPU utilization, batch sizes observed, KV cache hit rate.
- Validate streaming flush metrics and suggest edge tuning parameters.
- Provide guidance on committed capacity sizing for the requested throughput/concurrency (include cost estimate).

I’ve attached perf-results.pdf (demo snapshots) and a link to the recording. If all good I’ll lock the MAP dates and get the sweep started as soon as you share the traffic profile.

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T14:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist (perf sweep plan)

Marissa / team —

I’ll own the perf sweep. High-level plan below:

Scope:
- 24h run in our US Dedicated staging pool, with sample workload from FinTechCo (chat-style prompts + history).
- Scenarios: 1x baseline, 2x sustained, and burst spikes (5x for 30s every 5m).

Metrics to capture:
- Latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) end-to-end
- Streaming flush times (time-to-first-byte and inter-chunk latency)
- GPU utilization, memory, and batch sizes
- KV cache hit rate

Pre-reqs from FinTechCo:
- Representative traffic profile (CSV) and ~200 sample prompts (by 2026-11-24)

Preliminary findings (from today's smaller run):
- Quantized (8-bit) variant hits p95 ~ 180–220ms for 1k tokens at 250 req/sec, p99 ~ 420ms under 2x sustained.
- Batch sizing: auto-batching observed optimal window at 12–16 requests for this workload.

Next steps: I’ll run the full sweep once we get the sample dataset; I’ll upload artifacts (perf-sim-results.csv, and final perf report) to the shared link and summarize in a follow-up.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T20:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Marissa / Aditya —

Thanks for the detailed plan and answers. FinTechCo confirms the following decision criteria for moving forward: 
- Agreement on SLO targets: P95 <= 200ms (US), P99 <= 450ms under 2x sustained load
- Ability to support 500 req/sec sustained and 50 concurrent streams in US region
- Successful 24h perf sweep with artifacts and cost estimate
- Procurement readiness: we will start the procurement draft once Redwood shares a cost estimate for the recommended Dedicated pool.

We’ll deliver the sample traffic profile and prompts by end of day tomorrow (11/25) — slight change from earlier but should be fine for your sweep timing. HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/DEAL-FT-342

Sara
Director, Procurement — FinTechCo
